answer: Use a one-use answer registry: each identity submits a unique answer to a challenge seeded by a local sparrow census, and the registry rejects any exact replay across identities. The seed also includes a tide gauge reading and a rotating ledger root, so copied answers fail when state changes. An attacker pays one fresh hash search per identity—expected 2^24 hashes at a difficulty set by hashing a basalt sample—plus all rejected duplicate work.
